races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 2m1½f maiden hurdle on good-to-firm ground at Sligo is set to drift into a moderately-run affair with the pace controlled by whoever takes it up by default — likely one of the unknown-style runners such as Hey Sir, Returning Officer, or Unknown Fortune, none of whom have a clear front-running profile but may push forward simply to avoid being last. The absence of a genuine pace-setter on good-to-firm ground means fractions will be uneven, with a bunched mid-race before a sprint-style finish kicks off from the final turn — a test that will expose stamina limitations rather than reward pure closing kicks. The entire field is dominated by hold-up types, and with Boo Radley, Rosenborg, Middlethird Marvel, Tommy Go Maith, and Gethegoodtimesroll all naturally wanting to come from behind, the final half-mile will be an awkward scrimmage rather than a clean sweep. This shape favours whoever can secure a prominent mid-pack position and travel smoothly into the sprint — horses that can quicken off a slow pace with clean jumping will have the decisive edge over pure hold-up gallopers; the field holds more hold-up types than the race can accommodate at the rear, with A Mayo Breeze, Nile Star, Brother Hollie, Tribal, and Gethegoodtimesroll all redistributed — of these, Returning Officer and Hey Sir are most likely to actually press forward and secure a tactical position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race drifts at a false gallop and becomes a bunched sprint from the final hurdle
scenarios.body: With no front-runner to set genuine fractions on good-to-firm ground, the field compresses into a tight pack and the winner will be the horse that quickens fastest off a slow pace; prominent-tracking types with a sharp turn of foot hold the strongest hand here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknown-style horses pushes forward early and controls a steady tempo to the last
scenarios.body: A controlled front-running display at an honest but not brutal gallop would suit a horse able to jump fluently and stay on strongly on good-to-firm; the winner would be a mid-pack tracker who picks off the leader approaching the last.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly from halfway and genuine hold-up runners are able to find clear daylight late
scenarios.body: Despite the redistribution of several natural hold-up types into midfield on the map, Boo Radley and Rosenborg are true closers who could benefit if the race truly develops a strong gallop; however this scenario is discounted because the field's genuine hold-up horses are racing out of role and the closing kick in a bunched finish is unreliable here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Carnage Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart over the final hurdles with jumping errors causing interference that reshuffles the order
scenarios.body: On good-to-firm ground with maiden hurdlers, jumping errors late in the race could promote a latent staying type who survives the carnage; the winner in this shape would be a sturdy, uncomplicated jumper who keeps finding.

watchPoints.text: Returning Officer and Hey Sir are the two unknown-style runners most likely to fill the pace vacuum — watch at the start to see which one pushes forward, as whoever leads will have a significant tactical advantage in a sprint finish with no natural front-runner.

Boo Radley has the Mullins yard behind him after a 276-day absence, but watch for signs of freshness or rustiness at the first hurdle — if he jumps poorly he will be fighting the race shape from the outset.

Good-to-firm ground at Sligo will put a premium on clean jumping, and with seven horses carrying a fade-in-finish flag or a hold-up style that cannot be fulfilled, watch for a bunched finish over the last two hurdles where interference is a real risk.

Nile Star and A Mayo Breeze both ran just nine days and 261 days ago respectively — the contrast in freshness between these redistributed hold-up types is worth monitoring as the race develops, since neither is well positioned in the race shape regardless of fitness.

races.paceDynamic: Beat The Devil is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner maiden hurdle on Good to Firm ground at Sligo, and with no rival likely to press hard for the lead, the pace should be controlled and sustainable rather than frenetic. Behind the leader, Hygge, Manoir De Mirande, and Whats New are genuine prominent types who will track close to the speed, creating a compact early order that could compress the field and limit the scope for late closers. The hold-up brigade — Casheldale Lass, Bobby Kirova, Pebble Island, and I'm All In — will need the pace to collapse in the home straight to make meaningful late ground, which is less likely given a single uncontested leader on fast ground. This shape clearly favours prominent racers who can travel smoothly just off Beat The Devil and produce a clean jump at the last, with the off-the-pace types at a structural disadvantage unless the leader sets a genuinely strong gallop. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically operate deep in the field; Georg Zhukov is a genuine hold-up horse displaced to midfield on the map, and Beat The Devil is shown in the prominent zone despite its primary role as the leader, meaning both are mapped out of their natural territory.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Beat The Devil dictates a measured gallop and prominent trackers like Hygge or Manoir De Mirande travel smoothly before striking from two out.
scenarios.body: Beat The Devil sets a contained pace that rewards horses travelling with cover just behind, and the Good to Firm surface keeps the race from turning into a stamina grind that suits deep closers. Hygge's consistent placed form and Manoir De Mirande's recent course-distance profile make them the primary beneficiaries of this most likely shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Beat The Devil is allowed to stride clear from the front and the prominent horses fail to close the gap on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With no pressure on the leader and a fast-topped surface rewarding fluency, an uncontested Beat The Devil can dictate every yard and still have reserves for the finish. This scenario is realistic given the confirmed absence of any natural front-running rival to force the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than expected and the lead horses tie up in the final stages, allowing the hold-up runners to close.
scenarios.body: Casheldale Lass has solid placed form on similar going and Pebble Island has shown placed form at the trip, giving them the best closing profiles if the front end weakens. However, this scenario is structurally less likely given a lone, uncontested front-runner on fast ground who has no reason to overextend.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Steal The Show
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unexposed runners — Emmamia, Megaball, or Sylvie Power — produces a performance well above their profile on debut.
scenarios.body: An unexposed horse carrying unknown ability can disrupt any predicted race shape, and Gordon Elliott's Noble Rocco and the Irish handler-trained newcomers have each shown only glimpses so far. This scenario is the least structured and hardest to predict, reserved for a genuine upset from an unknown quantity.

watchPoints.text: Hygge is the most consistent performer in this field with four consecutive placed runs and two similar-going wins — watch for Gordon Elliott's team to have her travelling sweetly off the pace through the early stages before pressing from two out.

Beat The Devil's uncontested lead is the key structural variable — if anything flukes its way to the front or challenges early, the entire pace dynamic shifts and hold-up horses gain a material chance.
Manoir De Mirande ran just six days ago; watch for any signs of a hard race on that occasion and monitor market moves as a guide to whether Elliott sends him out fresh or as a prep.

Georg Zhukov carries a 98-day absence and is a genuine hold-up type compressed further forward on the map than natural — watch whether the jockey attempts to drop him out early and whether that creates traffic issues in a 14-runner field.

Three Gordon Elliott runners (Hygge, Manoir De Mirande, Noble Rocco) create an interesting team dynamic — watch which receives the stronger market support as a pointer to which Elliott considers his primary chance.

runners_data.name: Kenisa Sport
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 120 returning from a 290-day absence; has two wins from four runs in similar going, genuine front-runner who sets her own pace, but the fitness query after nearly ten months off is the one significant doubt and Joshua Halford's 7lb claim partially offsets the weight.
runners_data.comment: Won two and three starts back, then faded to fifth last time out, with two wins in her last four starts marking solid recent form over today's distance. Rated 117, second in the field, she is a leading threat back after 290 days off.

runners_data.name: Beauforts Storm
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who was last seen 12 days ago (fresh, quick reappearance); inconsistent form string (5-772U) though placed in Good going and stays the trip, will need a stronger gallop than likely to get competitive from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, though runner-up two starts back and has raced over today's distance before. Top-rated in the field at 117, she remains a leading contender on figures, but unseating last time out, 12 days ago, is the obvious blot.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: Returned to form with a win and a third in her last two starts; genuine hold-up type wearing a hood, won over 16f in Good — ground is fine but she'll need to produce a strong late run on a circuit that can be unforgiving for closers.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out - her only success in the last five starts - and she has already run over today's distance. Rated 115, above her official mark of 113, she's a solid case on that improving profile, with a 44-day layoff since the sole concern.

runners_data.name: Our Lucky Lady
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with three wins in Good or similar going, including over course-relevant distances; fitted with a hood, the 72-day break (with a schooling flat race 32 days ago) keeps her fresh, and her record shows she handles this pace scenario well tracking close to the leader.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back, then runner-up two starts back, before fading to ninth last time out - one win in her last four starts. She has form over today's distance, but rated below her official mark of 111 at 106, suggesting more to find.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent, very recent run (8 days ago), trainer has 0 from 16 over the past 14 days which is a concern; has struggled at longer trips (pulled up and unseated in recent starts) but reverts to a more suitable 2m trip here.
runners_data.comment: Rated above her official mark, 111 to 108, and freshly raced just 8 days ago with form over today's distance. But recent starts are mixed - fifth last time out and unseated two back - for only one win in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a tongue-tie; best form came at shorter trips (wins around 9-10f on flat) and stepping back up to 18f hurdles has returned mixed results — the trip is a potential query on fast ground at this track.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in her last four starts, but competitive on her best form: third two starts back, then fourth three starts back, and she has form over today's distance. Rated a shade above her official mark, 105 to 103, a 61-day absence since is the query.

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Long-term absentee returning after 444 days (with a flat run 22 days ago as a prep); naturally races at the front but this field pushes her further back than she'd like, and the layoff combined with competing against more active rivals makes it hard to trust on reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last five starts, with a pulled-up and a ran-out among the finishes, and the yard is out of form at 1/27 this fortnight. She was runner-up three and four starts back, though, and does have form over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Crystabel

runners_data.name: Doyen Magic
runners_data.note: Held-up type whose best form (two seconds) came in Yielding or Soft conditions at Haydock; Good to Firm at Sligo is quicker than anything in her recent record and that going concern, combined with her hold-up style, makes her reliant on a scenario that is unlikely to unfold.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our weights at 98, and yet to win in her last five starts, following an unplaced effort last time out. She was runner-up three and four starts back, though, and does have form over today's distance.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Front-running type by nature but redistribution means she faces a race run against her grain; trainer has 2 from 18 over the last 14 days showing some form, and the mare's best form is at shorter trips (12-14f) — stepping to 2m1½f on fast ground is a compounding question.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last four starts, but the form is on the up - two eighths preceded a fourth last time out - and she has form over today's distance. Rated above her official mark, 100 to 91, there's a sliver of encouragement here.

races.paceDynamic: Kenisa Sport is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger likely to contest the lead, she can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Sligo. Behind her, Our Lucky Lady, Radar Ahead, and Keilah are all natural prominent racers who will press for position just off the pace, creating a compact, moderately-paced early shape rather than a true test. The field contains more prominent-racing types than can realistically hold that position: Albatala, Crystabel, and Steps In The Sand are all genuine front-rank horses by nature but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because Kenisa Sport, Our Lucky Lady, Radar Ahead, and Keilah are most likely to secure the forward slots ahead of them. With a single uncontested leader setting a measured tempo, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who travel close to the pace throughout and have the class and ground-speed to quicken on a flat, fast-ground circuit — hold-up horses tracking from the rear face a longer run at it and must hope the pace honest enough to bring them into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kenisa Sport Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kenisa Sport leads unchallenged and sets a fair but undemanding tempo that stretches the field without burning herself out.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard from the front, with the prominent brigade of Our Lucky Lady, Radar Ahead, and Keilah tracking but never truly threatening her rhythm; on Good to Firm ground her class at OR 120 and proven front-running wins (2W in similar going) give her the advantage at the last. Horses who travel prominently throughout without overspending energy early are rewarded as the pace is never punishing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kenisa Sport's long absence (290 days) tells on her jumping or stamina and a prominent tracker swoops inside the final flight.
scenarios.body: Our Lucky Lady (three wins in similar going, OR 111, claiming rider) or Radar Ahead are ideally positioned to inherit the lead if the front-runner fades, having been travelling comfortably throughout without expending excess energy.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to stretch the field and create a true run-in for hold-up horses coming from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Splashing Out (recent form 1-3, won in Good going over a similar trip) and Beauforts Storm are the most credible closers, but they need things to fall perfectly and the controlled pace scenario makes this less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners overpace early and the whole field comes together turning for home in a scramble.
scenarios.body: A total unravelling of the front group would open the door for Doyen Magic or Steps In The Sand who are fresh (29 days) and carry lower weights, but this is a low-probability outcome given Kenisa Sport's likely ability to control the tempo unchallenged.

watchPoints.text: Kenisa Sport's 290-day absence is the single biggest race-changer — watch her jumping in the early stages for any sign of rustiness, as a blunder or loss of fluency could immediately rebalance the whole race shape and open the door for Our Lucky Lady.

Albatala, Crystabel, and Steps In The Sand are all naturally prominent horses squeezed into the midfield by this pace dynamic — if any of them breaks sharply and forces their way to the front, it could unexpectedly pressurise Kenisa Sport and turn a controlled pace into a contested one.

Radar Ahead ran just eight days ago — monitor whether that quick turnaround has blunted her edge, particularly as her OR 108 represents a step up in class versus recent runs and her trainer's 0/16 14-day record suggests yard form is flat.

Good to Firm ground is faster than anything Doyen Magic has encountered in her relevant form entries — if the going rides quicker than expected, watch for her to lose her place early and become irrelevant, confirming this as a pace-favouring surface.

Splashing Out (hood, hold-up) and Beauforts Storm are the only two true closers in the field — if either is seen travelling smoothly and making ground on the bridle approaching two out, it would be a strong signal that the gallop has been stronger than the pace map projects.

runners_data.note: Edward Cawley's mare is a genuine hold-up performer despite being mapped to midfield here due to field congestion at the rear; ran 35 days ago and has a second and a third in recent Good-ground starts, though 13 of 15 runs on similar ground hasn't produced consistent results and the 7lb claimer adds a risk element.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts and near bottom of our weights, though a second two starts back shows some ability, and he has form over today's distance. Rated just above his official mark, 103 to 100, with a seventh last time out.

runners_data.name: Phoenix Arizona
runners_data.note: Mapped to midfield but truly a hold-up type, which is confirmed by five consecutive races on Good or Soft all failing to produce a win; 8 of 9 runs on similar going with no wins is stark, the light 7lb claimer O'Connor is in maiden territory, and the OR of 90 represents the bottom of this handicap.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of the weights at 93 and yet to win in his last five starts, with two unplaced efforts in that sequence. He was runner-up five starts back and has form over today's distance, though only fourth last time out.

races.paceDynamic: Stormbreaker is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse genuinely likely to press from the front, sets up a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Sligo. Tell Us This, Bridgehead, and Dairy Force are the likeliest prominent companions, sitting just off the leader rather than challenging for the lead, which means Stormbreaker can dictate without significant early pressure. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their natural position — Maxwell Smart, Mary's Pride, and Phoenix Arizona are true pace/prominent horses pushed back into midfield by the volume of pace, meaning their chance is compromised by having to race out of role. This shape — a single leader setting a fair but uncontested tempo on fast ground over a sharp 2m1½f circuit — firmly favours hold-up horses who can travel smoothly in behind and produce a sustained run from two out, rewarding those with the class and fitness to close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stormbreaker Controls; Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Stormbreaker leads uncontested at a fair clip and the hold-up runners find clear air turning for home.
scenarios.body: Stormbreaker sets a measured pace that keeps the race honest without burning off the field, and the genuine hold-up performers who have been travelling in behind deliver their finishing efforts from the second-last flight; on Good to Firm ground this scenario rewards horses with proven form on similar going over this trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Tell Us This and Bridgehead push Stormbreaker harder than expected and the race is run at a genuine pace from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field and those racing prominently but with stamina reserves — particularly horses with recent course-and-distance form — are best placed to sustain their effort to the line; the hold-up horses may find the gaps shut or arrive too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse; Held-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Stormbreaker and the prominent horses go overly steady and the race becomes a sprint from the second-last.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race over a sharp Sligo circuit produces a messy finish where those positioned just off the pace in the first half of the field have the advantage, as acceleration from the rear is difficult when the tempo suddenly quickens; horses with a genuine turn of foot and recent sharp form benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Stormbreaker builds an unassailable lead and the closers are left with too much to do.
scenarios.body: Sligo's tight circuit and fast ground can occasionally allow a front-runner to steal an uncontested advantage that proves beyond catching, particularly if the hold-up horses are shuffled back or meet traffic; this is the least likely shape given the number of prominent types who will keep Stormbreaker honest.

watchPoints.text: Wolf Prince's 807-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if Aidan Melia has him ready to fire first time back, the hold-up profile and Good-going form make him dangerous, but any sign of rustiness and he will be found out on this sharp circuit.

Maxwell Smart, Mary's Pride, and Phoenix Arizona are all natural pace or hold-up horses who will be competing for fewer natural positions than their instincts demand — watch for bumping and shuffling as the tape rises, which could compromise several runners' runs simultaneously.

Dairy Force's 10-day turnaround for Gordon Elliott is worth monitoring in the paddock; fit horses can go quickly back to the well at this level but the hood and a pattern of placed efforts without winning raises the question of whether he finds a way to win today.

Tell Us This is the form anchor of the race — a course-and-distance winner 51 days ago on Good ground with a prominent style that should see him positioned perfectly; his chance holds across multiple scenarios and he is the reference point for what a winning time will require.

Good to Firm ground at Sligo will place a premium on jumping fluency — the sharp circuit punishes even a minor jumping error at pace, and runners with jumping concerns (Stormbreaker's long layoff, One Last Tango's pulled-up recent run) are worth watching carefully at the first few hurdles.

races.name: Kilcawley Construction Handicap Hurdle (0-100) (Div 2)

runners_data.name: Go To Town
runners_data.note: Unclassified style makes placement uncertain; seven runs on similar going without a win or place suggests this 6-year-old is struggling to find his level despite a top-end OR of 99, and 37 days since last run offers no freshness edge.
runners_data.comment: Three times fourth in his last five starts, he has been racing to a level that makes him our top-rated runner in this field, with form over today's distance and a return to fitness after 37 days off. Yet to win, but the clear form pick.

runners_data.name: Cherry Red
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up operator who won over 18f on Good last time and is placed again this trip; Ben Harvey takes over but the ⚠ fade flag is a consistent pattern and a slow pace will leave her with nothing to run into.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out 33 days ago, bouncing back from two pulled-up efforts and one unseated in the three starts before that. Carries 165lb and our figures peg her a solid midfield contender rather than one of the leading players here.

runners_data.name: Lilac Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with four places from 15 similar-going runs; Alan King claims 7lb which helps at the weights, but she has never won on Good and may need a stronger pace than Poppycon is likely to set.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without winning, with two thirds and a second among her last five starts, most recently fourth 33 days ago. Our figures make her a fair midfield performer in this field, but she needs more to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Papagei
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with limited comparable going form (6 from 15 on similar); Harry Sexton claims 7lb and the 60-day absence is a mild query in a competitive 18-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Fourth on his latest start and fifth before that, after a fall three runs back. Has form over today's trip and our figures make him competitive off his mark, but he is winless of late and a 60-day break is the query.

runners_data.name: Poppycon
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and confirmed pace-setter; she won over 16f on Soft but has only two runs on similar going so the fast ground is a mild unknown — her STYLE_FIT flag notes she may be racing slightly out of role in a race with this many runners pressing behind.
runners_data.comment: A second three starts back shows he retains real ability, and our figures make him one of the leading dangers here. He has form over today's distance and returns from a 43-day break, though a fall two starts back is the risk attached.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner suited by a prominent position over this trip; trainer John McConnell had no wins from 10 runners in the last 14 days and Fine Print has one place from eight similar-going runs — solid pace presence but limited winning form.
runners_data.comment: Well held in each of his last five starts, with finishes no better than fourth and a ninth among them, leaving him hard to fancy on these figures. He carries 155lb and our figures peg him a backmarker in this field, ranked 14th of 18.

runners_data.name: Poetic Focus
runners_data.note: Unclassified style and only 8 days since last run, which is a notable freshness concern; Andrew Slattery's stable is in fair recent form (3/27 T14) and the horse has placed on Good but has not won in this company.
runners_data.comment: Fifth on her latest start, one of a run of modest efforts - seventh before that and an unplaced effort prior, plus a fall four back. Returns quickly after 8 days over a proven trip; our figures make her a fair midfield sort but she is winless lately.

runners_data.name: Saint Peregrine
runners_data.note: Hold-up handler with three places from 15 similar-going runs but placed 13th twice at this track's distance equivalent; J J Slevin is a strong booking yet the form string 37F00 offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Our figures rate him a striking 11lb above his official mark of 86, making him one of the leading dangers in this field. He has raced over today's distance and returns fit after 33 days, though two unplaced efforts in his last two starts are the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Larkins Lane
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at OR 85 on Good and Soft over 20f; Shane O'Callaghan claims 3lb and the trainer P J Rothwell is in sharp 14-day form (3/28) — prominent style fits this race shape well and the course distance suits.
runners_data.comment: Won her last two starts after finishes of ninth, eighth and fifth before that, but our figures rate her well below her official mark, at just 79, 16th of 18 in this field. Plenty to find on these figures despite the recent brace.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type by nature whose finishing fade flag and OR-84 rating limit appeal; placed into midfield because the field is saturated with rear-of-field horses, meaning she is likely to race forward of her ideal position and her late run may be blunted.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of her last five starts, including three unplaced efforts, leaving little to recommend her on these figures. Our figures rate her a shade above her official mark at 85, but she remains one of the more workmanlike sorts in this field, 13th of 18.

runners_data.name: Tellmemamema
runners_data.note: All five similar-going runs have been placed in the top half without a win; Tom Buckley takes over but the ⚠ fade flag and redistribution out of true hold-up role combine to make this an each-way outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence - fifth and fourth in her last two starts, preceded by two unplaced efforts - leaves her firmly midfield on these figures. She has raced over today's distance before, and our figures rate her a touch above her official mark, at 87.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: 112 days off the track is the standout concern; I Madden's yard has no 14-day runners to reference, tongue-tie fitted, and the horse's best finish on comparable going was 7th — a major absence flag in a competitive field.
runners_data.comment: His last run, a ninth, is the standout concern coming after a 112-day absence, in a recent sequence that also included a fall two starts back. Our figures rate him well above his official mark at 89, but that lengthy layoff leaves obvious fitness questions.

runners_data.name: Mr Erwitt
runners_data.note: 267 days absent is an extreme layoff flag for a hold-up horse with a P-P finish string; even placed into midfield on the map, this is a horse whose race fitness must be seriously questioned and the ⚠ fade flag compounds the doubt.
runners_data.comment: His last two starts both ended in a pulled-up effort, the most recent 267 days ago, following finishes of ninth and fourth before that. Too little recent evidence to trust him on these figures, and that lengthy absence adds a significant fitness question mark.

runners_data.name: Finnicky Filly
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style mare, six runs between 5th and 6th on similar going with one career place on Good; Daniel King rides and the Ryan yard is in active recent form, making her a solid if unspectacular pace presence.
runners_data.comment: A modest sequence of fifths and sixths dominates her recent form, with a second five starts back the best of them. Our figures match her official mark exactly at 78, ranked 17th of 18 in this field, and she has plenty to find to trouble these rivals.

runners_data.name: Sekifi
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted, ⚠ fade flag and only a 5th from nine similar-going runs; Michael Kenneally claims 5lb but this 8-year-old has never finished in the first four at a comparable level on Good ground and the redistribution away from true hold-up position doesn't help.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence including two unplaced efforts leaves little to recommend him on paper, though our figures rate him some way above his official mark, at 79. He has raced over today's distance before, but sits among the outsiders in this field, ranked 15th of 18.

runners_data.name: Mother Ship
runners_data.note: No jockey listed which is a notable market concern; hold-up type with three places from 15 similar-going runs, pushed into midfield because of field saturation — Hanlon has two runners in this race and this is likely the second string.
runners_data.comment: A second five starts back is the highlight of a mixed recent sequence that also includes a pulled-up run and two eighths. She has raced over today's distance before, and our figures rate her a shade above her official mark, leaving her a fair midfield sort in this field.

runners_data.name: Ladiam
runners_data.note: No jockey listed, but the form profile is strong: one win and six places from 15 similar-going runs, consecutive 5ths at this distance on Good, tongue-tie worn, and a prominent style that fits the likely race shape — one of the most interesting profiles despite the jockey absence.
runners_data.comment: Placed third four starts back, and runner-up five starts back, she looks a leading danger - our figures put her above her official mark of 92. Proven over the trip; the query is back-to-back fifths of late, and she stays winless.

runners_data.name: Cornaroya Rocco
runners_data.note: Hold-up type from the Hanlon yard (also trains Mother Ship); five runs on similar going without a win, placed 4th last time over 16f on Good, and stepping up from shorter distances — needs to prove the 2m4f trip suits.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time out, though the form before that reads more solidly with fourth, fifth and sixth across his last three starts prior. Our figures peg him a shade below his official mark at 92, leaving him a fair, if unspectacular, midfield contender in this field.

races.paceDynamic: Poppycon is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner handicap hurdle over 2m4f at Sligo, and with no horse genuinely threatening to push her across the line she is set to control proceedings at a sustainable, uncontested tempo on Good to Firm ground. Fine Print, Larkins Lane, and Ladiam are the natural prominent types who will track closely, creating a compact lead group rather than a strung-out gallop, which keeps the pace honest without becoming scorching. The field is overloaded with hold-up horses — Mother Ship, Frontier Rose, Tellmemamema, Dream Shaper, Mr Erwitt, and Sekifi are all genuine rear-of-field operators who have been mapped to midfield simply because there is insufficient room at the back for all of them, meaning several will race out of their preferred position and their finishing kicks may be compromised. This controlled, single-pace scenario strongly favours horses racing prominently or in close pursuit of the leader, specifically those with the stamina to sustain a forward position into the straight without being softened by a genuine searching gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Poppycon Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Poppycon bowls along at a controlled clip unchallenged and prominent trackers conserve energy to pounce from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Poppycon sets a manageable tempo that suits horses sitting second or third who can produce a clean jump at the last two flights and pick her off on the run-in; on Good to Firm ground at Sligo the leader rarely survives if a well-placed chaser has petrol left. Larkins Lane and Ladiam, both experienced prominent racers with Sligo-suitable profiles and good good-ground records, are the types whose chance is maximised in this controlled-pace shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Poppycon Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly uncontested and the prominent trackers fail to make up ground turning for home on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Poppycon dictates every yard, the field strings out late, and no single challenger has enough momentum off a slow gallop to collar her in time; her OR of 94 and a course that suits front-runners who can dictate on a flat-ish circuit makes this a live threat. The Good to Firm conditions help a front-runner conserve energy through the early stages and have enough left for the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the back straight to flatten the prominent horses and a well-placed midfield runner has the class to pick through.
scenarios.body: Cherry Red or Lilac Lady, racing just off the pace, could benefit if the leaders tire on the flat of the final circuit and a surge from the rear materialises; Cherry Red won last time out over 18f on Good and retains claims if her finishing fade is managed by a confident hold-up ride from Ben Harvey. This scenario is modestly discounted because several natural hold-up horses have been displaced into midfield and may not deliver the late thrust their style implies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Genuine Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If pace is strong enough to burn off the lead group and a true hold-up horse survives the traffic in an 18-runner field to unleash a late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands the pace to be genuinely fierce, which the race shape does not support given a single uncontested front-runner; horses like Frontier Rose, Tellmemamema, and Mother Ship are natural rear-of-field types but are mapped forward and are racing partially out of role, materially reducing the likelihood of a clean late delivery. The probability is heavily discounted because the horses who would win this shape are not guaranteed to secure their ideal position.

watchPoints.text: Larkins Lane is the prominent horse whose back-to-back wins and active trainer form make her the most dangerous in the likely race shape — watch if she travels sweetly in third or fourth from the outset.
Ladiam holds a strong similar-going profile and a prominent style that fits perfectly; the absence of a declared jockey is the only cloud and must be monitored before the off.
Mother Ship and Ladiam both have no jockey listed — if either is a non-runner or takes a conditional jockey at short notice, the market and race shape both shift.
Mr Erwitt (267 days off) and Dream Shaper (112 days off) are major fitness queries; if either shows unexpected market support it would be a significant stable confidence signal worth noting.

Watch the early gallop rate from Poppycon — if Fine Print or Larkins Lane push up and force a quicker tempo than expected, the race shape flips from a slow-pace prominent benefit to a genuine test of stamina that could open the door for Cherry Red or Lilac Lady.

races.name: Sligo Park Hotel Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Kalanisi Flash
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner, has the race to himself on a Good to Firm surface that he handles (7W5P in similar going), but 74 days off and a tongue-tie return for a yard 1/22 in the last fortnight are caution flags; controls the race shape but winning it from the front over 3m1½f is another matter.
runners_data.comment: Kalanisi Flash won four starts back, then third three starts back, before pulling up in each of his last two starts. He is off 74 days for a yard managing just 1 from 22 recently, the obvious concern for a gelding we rate at 113.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for Noel Meade who has finished no better than sixth in his last six starts and carries the ⚠ fade-in-finish flag; 52 days since last run, all five recent efforts on Good ground have been modest, and this big field is unlikely to suit.
runners_data.comment: Golden Temple has been well held in each of his last five starts, without a win in that sequence. He returns after 52 days off rated 109 with us, matching his 109 official mark, and a switch back to sharper form would make him relevant again.

runners_data.name: Streets Of Doyen
runners_data.note: 12-year-old hold-up runner with genuine staying credentials (34f and 28f runs in history), handles Good ground, but form figures of 45P9 and a big field at this trip stretch credibility; one-pace grinder who needs a truly strong gallop.
runners_data.comment: Streets Of Doyen already has form over today's trip and, on our figures, rates a striking 21lb above his 105 official mark. His last two runs (9th, pulled up) are modest, but with a 4th and 5th before that, and just 35 days since his latest start, he's the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a Good-ground win at 26f on his CV and three course-distance wins in the book; 181 days off (70 days on Flat) is a real concern, but the trip and going are squarely in his wheelhouse if fitness holds.
runners_data.comment: Cornmarket won three starts back but the form has since dipped, falling next time out and finishing 8th last time. He does have form over today's trip, though our figures place him 5lb below his 102 official mark, suggesting he has more to find.

runners_data.name: Evans Secret
runners_data.note: Prominent type with a striking Good-ground record (11/15) and back-to-back 26f wins in recent form; Darragh O'Keeffe in the saddle adds significant confidence, and this horse appears among the best placed to actually secure the prominent position it wants.
runners_data.comment: Evans Secret won two starts back, then a good second last time out, form that has him rated 100 with us, matching his official mark. A break of 61 days is the query, though he does have form over today's trip to fall back on.

runners_data.name: Justatan
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Emmet Mullins returning after 168 days off; predominantly a shorter-trip horse (16-18f history) stepping up sharply to 3m1½f, and the Good to Firm going is rare territory — only 1 run from 5 on similar ground.
runners_data.comment: Justatan was third three starts back but the placings have since gone the wrong way, unplaced two starts back, and only ninth last time out. A lengthy 168-day absence adds to the concerns, and our figures already have him 4lb below his 100 official mark.

runners_data.name: Sphagnum
runners_data.note: Prominent-style stayer with two wins at 26f on Good ground in his recent history and a strong similar-going record (12/15); headgear (blinkers) suggests a freshener is needed to keep him honest, and this trip at Sligo suits.
runners_data.comment: Sphagnum bounced back to finish second last time out, leaving him rated 19lb above his 100 official mark on our figures. That followed a moderate run of finishes, so confirming that effort is the key question, though a 33-day turnaround and trip form are in his favour.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who ran just 10 days ago, showing no ill-effects last time; 14 out of 15 runs on Good ground underlines extreme suitability to conditions, though has not won in this form cycle and is a place horse more than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Smallcraftwarning was runner-up just 10 days ago, form that has him rated 7lb above his 96 official mark on our figures. The formline before that is patchy — 8th, 3rd, 8th and a pulled-up effort — though he does have form over today's trip.

runners_data.name: Je Suis
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for S Curling who briefly shows in midfield; Good-ground form is solid (10/12) and he was placed last time at this trip, but a 17-horse field and a moderate pace makes his late challenge hard to execute.
runners_data.comment: Je Suis was third last time out, her best effort in a modest recent sequence that also includes a pulled-up run and finishes no better than 6th. She sits just above her 95 official mark on our figures at 98, with form over today's trip in her favour.

runners_data.name: Kazbek
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 173 days off for Peter Fahey; limited Good-ground experience (1 from 7 runs) and the extended trip is new territory — too many unknowns after a long absence.
runners_data.comment: Kazbek was in good form when third and then second, before a dip that included two pulled-up efforts, the latest 173 days ago. He's rated 6lb above his 95 official mark on our figures, though the long absence and recent form are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Tango Theatre
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with Good-ground course form including a win at 26f; aged 11 but consistent on this surface (11/15), and trainer McConnell has a 1/30 strike rate in the last two weeks — form is there but connections are cold.
runners_data.comment: Tango Theatre won four starts back, and runner-up five starts back, but her form has since dipped with three below-par runs in her last three starts. She is rated a touch above her 94 mark on our figures at 97, though the yard is out of form of late.

runners_data.name: Wild Mandate
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for the McNiff yard with a decent Good-ground record (13/14); the shorter trips in his history (18-21f) make this 3m1½f test a step up in stamina, though he placed at 19f on similar terms recently.
runners_data.comment: Wild Mandate was runner-up three starts back but has otherwise struggled, with 9th, 7th, unplaced and 5th filling out her recent form. She rates a shade above her 91 official mark on our figures, though a mid-table finish is about the level, with plenty to find on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Joe's Turn
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer by nature whose preference for a forward position will be frustrated in this overloaded field — likely to be shuffled back against his instincts; has the Good-ground trip form (wins at 24-25f) but racing out of role tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Joe's Turn won four starts back, then second three starts back, but a fall and a well-beaten eighth in his last two have undone that promise. He is rated only a pound above his 89 official mark on our figures, and he needs a big step forward from here.

runners_data.name: Ballagh Star
runners_data.note: Front-running type who wants to race prominently but is mapped to midfield because the field cannot accommodate all the pace — likely held up against his will; has won at 26f on Good ground but recent form shows a string of non-completions and a last-time 0.
runners_data.comment: Ballagh Star won four starts back, and runner-up five starts back, but he has pulled up in two of his last three, including last time out. He rates 9lb above his 82 official mark on our figures, so the ability looks there, but recent form is a real concern.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Another true prominent racer who the race shape pushes into a midfield slot; recent form is solid (412) with wins and places at 25-26f on Good, and Noel Kelly's yard is 1/7 in 14 days — if he can force his way forward he is live, but the redistribution is a real handicap.
runners_data.comment: Le Grand Vert is in strong recent form, a winner two starts back, and a good second last time out just 16 days ago. That leaves him rated a striking 21lb above his 82 official mark on our figures, a huge shift after two modest fourths and a pulled-up run earlier in his form.

runners_data.name: Strong Contender
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who ends up shuffled further back than the map suggests; a 5-year-old returning 27 days after last run, with most form at shorter trips (16-17f), and limited Good-ground experience — the trip and race shape look against him.
runners_data.comment: Strong Contender was third five starts back but the form has gone backwards since - a fall four starts back, two unplaced efforts, and seventh last time out. She rates just a pound above her 81 official mark on our figures, and there is a lot to find from here.

runners_data.name: Back The West
runners_data.note: Persistent prominent type who is likely to be denied his natural position in this field; form of 759PP is concerning, no trainer/jockey listed (no declaration confirmation), and the 52-day absence combined with age (11) and recent failures makes this a very hard ride.
runners_data.comment: Back The West has pulled up in each of his last two starts, with a 9th, 5th and 7th further back in the form. He does rate 6lb above his 72 official mark on our figures, but he has a mountain to climb from here.

races.paceDynamic: Kalanisi Flash is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and should lead from the outset over this 3m1½f trip at Sligo on Good to Firm ground, setting a controlled, sustainable tempo with no genuine rival willing or able to challenge for the lead. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types — Evans Secret, Cornmarket, Sphagnum, Smallcraftwarning, Tango Theatre and Wild Mandate — will jostle for early position in the first few furlongs, creating pressure in the chasing group even if the leader himself travels easily. The field contains significantly more front-running and prominent-minded horses than can all secure their natural position; Joe's Turn, Ballagh Star, Le Grand Vert and Back The West are all genuine prominent racers who are likely to be shuffled back against their wishes, with Evans Secret and Sphagnum — both with strong Good-ground form at this sort of trip — best placed to actually sit where they want. With one honest pace-setter dictating an even gallop over a searching trip, this race shape favours resolute, prominent-to-midfield types who can travel comfortably just off the leader and sustain their effort through the final mile, rather than hold-up horses who will face a wall of traffic in a big field on a tight circuit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kalanisi Flash Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Kalanisi Flash leads at a fair clip and the chasing pack burns each other out competing for the prominent positions behind him.
scenarios.body: The solo front-runner dictates terms unchallenged on a Good to Firm surface that suits his form profile, and the field strings out as the prominent brigade traffic-jams behind; horses that travel smoothly just off the pace inherit the race when the scramblers tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types War
scenarios.trigger: If the displaced prominent runners — Joe's Turn, Le Grand Vert and Ballagh Star — force their way forward and push the early pace beyond Kalanisi Flash's comfort zone.
scenarios.body: A contested gallop from the front quickens the race up early and raises the toll on anything racing keenly in the first third; horses with the class and stamina to sit just off a hot pace and still find in the straight benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave the rear genuinely detached, creating a true end-to-end stamina test.
scenarios.body: Hold-up horses that have been squeezed to the back against their will would need an unusually flat-out gallop to make ground across 3m1½f at Sligo; Streets Of Doyen, with the right sort of trip form, and Je Suis could theoretically benefit but the conditions for this are narrow given no truly front-running pace battle is expected.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a moderate tempo that compacts the field into a bunch, turning the finish into a rough, attritional scramble.
scenarios.body: A messy, compressed finish in a 17-runner field on a tight circuit favours horses with course experience and tactical adaptability; runners tagged as redistributed out-of-role types will struggle to find daylight but those with previous Sligo or sharp-track form may be able to weave through.

watchPoints.text: Cornmarket's 181-day absence (including 70-day Flat break) is the single biggest risk factor — watch the market move in the final hour; if he drifts, fitness is suspect and his prominent role becomes a liability.

The opening half-mile is where the race could be made or broken: Joe's Turn, Le Grand Vert, Ballagh Star and Back The West will all attempt to push forward against their redistributed positions, creating a traffic scramble that could unsettle Evans Secret and Sphagnum.

Kalanisi Flash's 74-day lay-off and tongue-tie return under an apprentice (Dylan Kidd 7lb) for a yard striking at 1/22 in 14 days — if he idles or is caught cold at the start, the race loses its only confirmed pace anchor and turns chaotic.

Golden Temple carries the ⚠ fade-in-finish tag and is a hold-up horse in a big field at 3m1½f — watch for him to be outpaced before the home turn if the pace is honest; his recent record of six consecutive non-placed runs suggests he is vulnerable.

Smallcraftwarning ran just 10 days ago — monitor for any market drift that might signal a quick turnaround concern, but if fresh enough his exceptional Good-ground record (14/15) makes him worth tracking through the race as a place benchmark.

runners_data.name: Allez Yeats
runners_data.comment: Allez Yeats is unraced, so there's no form to judge her on. Everything is open to interpretation on debut, and with a first competitive test to come, she looks fully unexposed and capable of more than we currently know.

runners_data.name: Carleys Lilly
runners_data.comment: Carleys Lilly's last two starts read 4th and then 9th, the latter 45 days ago. She's been lightly campaigned in recent form and sits 6th of 12 on our figures at 87, leaving obvious questions given how little we've seen of her lately.

runners_data.name: Churchfield Annie
runners_data.comment: Churchfield Annie has three places from her last four starts, including a 3rd last time out, interrupted only by a pulled-up effort. She sits 4th of 12 on our figures at 90, has form over today's trip, and remains yet to win in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Circus Hill
runners_data.comment: Circus Hill has been admirably consistent, finishing 2nd, 4th, 4th and 2nd in her last four starts before a 6th further back, and tops our figures in this field on a rating of 96. She has form over today's trip, though she remains without a win in that sequence.

runners_data.name: Clovelly Charm
runners_data.comment: Clovelly Charm's form figures show just a 5th last time out, yet that's enough to see her rated 94 and 3rd of 12 in this field. She already has form over today's trip, and with more experience to follow there should be scope for improvement, though she remains largely unproven.

runners_data.name: Hill Of Ballyline
runners_data.comment: Hill Of Ballyline is unraced and makes her debut with no form to judge her on. She's fully unexposed, and while there's nothing concrete to build a case on, she could easily improve with racing experience once she gets a competitive introduction under her belt.

runners_data.name: Lexenna
runners_data.comment: Lexenna's recent form shows a 6th, 45 days ago, so there's little to judge her on yet. She remains unexposed at this stage, with room for progress on that outing.

runners_data.name: Maple Mornin
runners_data.comment: Maple Mornin is unraced and steps into this field with no form on the board. She's unexposed and hard to assess on debut, but with a first competitive run to come there's plenty of scope for her to show more than we currently know.

runners_data.name: Mila Ballerina
runners_data.comment: Mila Ballerina's recent form reads unplaced twice, the latest just 8 days ago, leaving little to go on yet. She remains unexposed at this stage, with a quick turnaround suggesting she's fit enough to build on that experience.

runners_data.name: Moyneard
runners_data.comment: Moyneard has been the essence of consistency, never finishing worse than 5th in her last five starts, rounding off with a 3rd last time out. Second of 12 on our figures at 94, she has form over today's trip, without a win yet to her name.

runners_data.name: Saoirses Choice
runners_data.comment: Saoirses Choice was 4th two starts back but dropped away to 9th last time out. Rated 87 and 5th of 12 on our figures, the recent downward step makes her hard to fancy on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Wild Eagle
runners_data.comment: Wild Eagle's recent form shows two unplaced efforts sandwiching an 8th, the latest 33 days ago. She remains lightly raced with limited evidence to judge her on, though there's time to progress with more experience.
